property_summary: For any deployed C, currentVersion() must return the oracle version with its price transformed by the product's payoffDefinition (i.e. equal to calling oracle().currentVersion() then applying payoffDefinition.transform); the mutant returns the raw oracle value (no transform) so for some oracle/pricing the returned price differs and the property fails.

For any deployed product C, currentVersion() returns the oracle currentVersion with its price transformed by the product's payoffDefinition; the mutant returns the raw oracle currentVersion (no transform) so for some oracle price the returned price will differ and the property is violated.

For all oracle-reported prices p, C.currentVersion() returns the oracle version with price transformed by the product's payoffDefinition (i.e. transformed price != raw price for some p); the mutant returns the raw oracle price so there exists an oracle price where the returned price differs and the property is violated.

For every oracle version returned, C.currentVersion() must return the oracle version whose price equals payoffDefinition.transform(oracle().currentVersion().price); the mutant returns the raw oracle.currentVersion() (no transform) so for some oracle price the returned price differs and the property is violated.

For every oracle-reported version, C.currentVersion() returns the oracle version with its price transformed by payoffDefinition.transform; the mutant returns the raw oracle version (no transform), so there exist oracle prices for which the returned price differs and the property is violated.

For any oracle state, C.currentVersion() returns the oracle's currentVersion() with its price transformed by payoffDefinition().transform(...) (i.e. price != ZERO for some oracle prices), whereas the mutant sets price to ZERO unconditionally, so there exists an oracle price where the reference's returned price differs from ZERO but the mutant returns ZERO.

For any oracle providing a nonzero price, C.currentVersion() returns an OracleVersion whose price is nonzero (payoffDefinition transforms it), but the mutant returns price == 0 for some oracle prices — so the reference's currentVersion().price != 0 for all nonzero oracle prices while the mutant can be zero.

For every oracle currentVersion() that returns without revert, C.currentVersion() returns a version whose price equals payoffDefinition.transform(original.price) (i.e. is not always zero); the mutant instead can return price == 0 for some oracle prices, so there exist inputs where C.currentVersion().price != 0 but the mutant's is 0.

For any deployed C, calling currentVersion() should return an OracleVersion whose price equals the transformed oracle price (i.e. not universally zero when the underlying oracle reports a non-zero price); the mutant returns price == 0 even when the underlying oracle reports a non-zero price, violating this rule for some oracle prices.

For any oracle-reported currentVersion.price, C.currentVersion() returns the oracle version with price transformed by the product's payoffDefinition (so when the oracle price is non-zero the returned price can be non-zero), whereas the mutant always returns price == ZERO — therefore there exists an oracle price input for which C.currentVersion().price != 0 but the mutant's is 0.

For any deployed product C, the stored maintenance parameter (set at initialize) is returned by maintenance(), whereas the mutant returns controller().minCollateral() which can differ; the test fuzzes an arbitrary minCollateral value and asserts that maintenance() equals the stored maintenance (which the correct contract always returns) — the mutant will fail when controller().minCollateral() != stored maintenance.

For any stored product maintenance value X and any controller minCollateral Y, the correct Product.maintenance() returns the stored X (independent of controller.minCollateral()); the mutant wrongly returns controller.minCollateral(), so when X != Y the mutant's maintenance() differs.

For any stored product maintenance value M (set during initialize) and any controller.minCollateral() value C, the correct contract's maintenance() always returns M; the mutant erroneously returns C, so when M != C the mutant's maintenance() differs.

For any controller and product initialization, the correct C.maintenance(account) always returns the product's stored maintenance parameter (independent of controller().minCollateral()), whereas the mutant returns controller().minCollateral(), so when those two values differ the mutant yields a different return value.

For any input, the reference contract returns its stored takerFee (which may be any UFixed18 ≤ ONE), whereas the mutant always returns UFixed18Lib.ONE — so the property is that c.takerFee() equals the stored pending/committed value (i.e. is not always ONE); the mutant violates this for inputs where the stored taker fee is not ONE.

For every admissible initial taker fee value passed into initialize, the correct contract's takerFee() returns that stored value (i.e. equals the initialized value), whereas the mutant always returns ONE and thus will differ whenever the initialized taker fee is not ONE.

For every initialized takerFee input (any UFixed18 value), the reference contract's takerFee() returns that stored value; the mutant always returns UFixed18Lib.ONE, so for some fuzzed initial takerFee inputs (those not equal to ONE) the mutant's takerFee() differs and the property is violated.

For any initialized productInfo.takerFee value, the correct contract's takerFee() returns that stored value (not always ONE); the mutant that hardcodes takerFee() to ONE will differ whenever the initialized takerFee != ONE.

For any initialized takerFee input, the reference contract returns that stored takerFee via its takerFee() getter; the mutant that hardcodes takerFee() to UFixed18Lib.ONE will return a different value whenever the initialized takerFee != ONE.

For any storage state of C, the public getter positionFee() returns exactly the stored _positionFee value (unmodified); the mutant that multiplies by 2 will return a different value for some stored _positionFee, so the property is violated for those inputs.

For any stored position fee value x, the contract's positionFee() returns exactly x (the stored UFixed18); the mutant that multiplies by 2 will return 2x for some fuzzed stored x, so the property is violated for those inputs.

For any stored positionFee value set via __UParamProvider__initialize during initialize(...), C.positionFee() returns that stored value (i.e., equals the initializer argument); the mutant doubling the returned value will cause inequality for some fuzzed initializer input.

For any UFixed18 value provided as the positionFee in ProductInfo during initialize, the contract's positionFee() getter returns that exact stored UFixed18; the mutant that multiplies the stored value by 2 will differ for some fuzzed initializer inputs (non-zero values).
